extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO staff, judges, policymakers, and legal scholars
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly, section-by-section legislative-history guide to the America Invents Act’s provisions that apply after a patent issues (post-grant review, inter partes proceedings, supplemental examination, prior-user rights, PTAB jurisdiction, PTE timing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holmes Group fix (Section 19(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends title 28 to clarify that state courts lack jurisdiction over legal claims arising under patent, copyright, and plant-variety-protection statutes; deems various overseas territories to be States for this purpose; extends the Federal Circuit’s appellate jurisdiction to compulsory patent and plant-variety-protection counterclaims (abrogating Holmes Group); and allows removal of civil actions in which “any party” asserts legal claims under those statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained as limiting forum-shopping and preserving uniformity of patent law; Senate amendment confined expanded jurisdiction to only compulsory counterclaims (Rule 13(a)) to prevent defendants from asserting unrelated counterclaims merely to manipulate appellate jurisdiction; §1454 modified to clarify intellectual-property counterclaims would not be remanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Circuit jurisdiction over PTAB proceedings (§1295(a)(4)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Revises §1295(a)(4)(A) to identify all Patent Trial and Appeal Board proceedings from which the Federal Circuit shall entertain appeals, including appeals from reexaminations and other PTAB actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate commentary notes language is generalized and clarified so details of appealability will be in sections 134 and 141; recognition of jurisdiction over reexaminations was made retroactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB redesignation and scope (35 U.S.C. §§6, 141)
rubrics_metrics.description: Redesignates the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (BPAI) as the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB); authorizes the Board to hear appeals of examinations and reexaminations; enables the Board to conduct derivation proceedings and inter partes and post-grant reviews; and modifies §141 to allow appeals of PTAB decisions in inter partes and post-grant reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows all members of the PTAB to participate in all proceedings (departure from earlier versions); effective-date provisions deem the PTAB to be the BPAI for pending interferences and extend existing appeal authorities to inter partes reexaminations commenced under the old system; references to derivation proceedings are deemed to extend to interferences commenced before repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeming provisions for pending interferences and reexaminations (§6(f)(2)(B), §7(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For pending interferences, the Director may deem the PTAB to be the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences and conduct any further proceedings; similar authority for pending inter partes reexaminations; language deems references to derivation proceedings to extend to interferences commenced before repeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to provide continuity for proceedings that began under the prior statutory scheme; ensures claims of pending matters are processed consistently during transition to new procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/exclusion from practice statute of limitations (35 U.S.C. §32, AIA §3(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifies statute of limitations for initiating a §32 proceeding to exclude an attorney from practice before the USPTO to require initiation within the earlier of either ten years after the misconduct occurred or one year after the misconduct was reported to the USPTO “as prescribed in ... regulations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the USPTO to report every two years to Congress on substantial incidents of misconduct that evade investigation because of the ten-year time limit; Senate proponents argued a 10-year limit balances accountability with reasonable recollection periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director intervention in appeals (35 U.S.C. §143, AIA §7(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends §143 to allow the Director to intervene in a Federal Circuit appeal of the PTAB’s decision in a derivation proceeding or in an inter partes or post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted in debates without extensive elaboration; provides USPTO leadership an express route to participate in appellate records concerning PTO-administered proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayh-Dole funding agreements and technical corrections (35 U.S.C. §202(b), AIA §13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduces the prior requirement that government-owned contractor-operated (GOCO) facilities pay 75% of royalty income in excess of 5% of annual budget to the government down to 15%; corrects minor errors, conforms statute to first-to-file system, and replaces a requirement to license federally-funded patented inventions to small firms with a 'preference' for small firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee report states change reduces disincentives for universities and small businesses to commercialize federally funded inventions; provides background on rationale from hearing testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee right to seek broadening reissue (35 U.S.C. §251, AIA §4(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends §251 to allow an assignee of a patent to seek a broadening reissue if the entire interest in the invention was assigned before the application for patent was filed; previously an assignee was barred from seeking broadening reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Still barred where assignee acquired patent/application from the inventor who filed the application; USPTO practice previously allowed some assignee-filed reissues where inventor did not oppose; Senate and House floor comments framed change as consistent with other expansions of assignee rights (e.g., §§115,118).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination (35 U.S.C. §257, AIA §12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes a new post-grant proceeding allowing the patent owner to submit any information believed to be 'relevant to the patent' to the USPTO; the Director must decide whether the information creates a substantial new question of patentability, and if so, the USPTO must reexamine the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary policy effect: if the Office determines that submitted information does not present a substantial new question or that the patent remains valid, that information cannot later be used to hold the patent unenforceable or invalid on the basis of inequitable-conduct attacks in civil litigation. Exceptions include prior allegations involving certain new drug applications (21 U.S.C. §355(j)) and instances where the patent owner has brought enforcement actions before the ITC or a U.S. district court unless the supplemental examination concluded before the action was brought. Subsection (e) requires referral to the Attorney General if the Director discovers a material fraud on the Office may have been committed. The Director 'shall' conduct supplemental examination; debate over whether referral decisions may be delegated to subordinates; proponents argued supplemental examination improves patent quality and investor confidence, critics warned it could 'immunize misconduct.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift of sanctioning responsibility to USPTO and sanction authority in post-grant proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA provisions expressly charge the USPTO with adopting regulations prescribing sanctions for abuse of discovery, abuse of process, or other improper uses of post-grant and inter partes proceedings (e.g., to harass or cause unnecessary delay or cost), and provide the Office tools to sanction misconduct (monetary fines, restrictive orders, dismissal, cancellation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate and reports framed this as shifting misconduct policing from Article III courts to the USPTO; proponents cited existing PTO inherent authority and regulatory sanctions; intended to deter abusive uses of new administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-user rights (35 U.S.C. §273, AIA §5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a broadened prior-user defense applicable to all utility patents: can be asserted for any process or for any product used in a manufacturing or other commercial process; to prevail, the defendant must show commercial use of the subject matter at least one year before the earlier of either the effective filing date of the claimed invention or a public disclosure that qualifies for the §102(b) grace period; defense applies only against patents issued on or after September 16, 2011; defense cannot be asserted against inventions made by a university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: House and Senate proponents argued the defense prevents incentive to offshore manufacturing and addresses policing difficulties for process patents; legislative history notes changes through floor amendments (e.g., elimination of reduction-to-practice requirement and clarification of who may assert the defense—'performed or directed the performance'). The Committee Report contained limited discussion and some elements changed after the report (so practitioners should read statutory text and floor remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-term extension timing rule (AIA §37 amending 35 U.S.C. §156)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies that if permission for commercial marketing or use of a product is received by the patentee on a weekend, a holiday, or after 4:30 P.M. Eastern Time on a business day, such permission will be deemed to have been received the next business day for purposes of patent-term extension filing deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to PTE applications pending on or after AIA enactment or subject to judicial review at enactment (retroactive effect); politically controversial 'special-fix' example: Angiomax patent-term-extension dispute—§37 rendered a previously late PTE application timely filed; floor debate highlighted concerns about special-interest lobbying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective-date and transitional rules for appeals and derivation references
rubrics_metrics.description: Language was added to deem references to derivation proceedings in current appeals statutes to extend to interferences commenced before the effective date of the AIA’s repeal of interferences; appeal authorities extended so they may continue to apply to inter partes reexaminations commenced under the old system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide continuity for pending matters during transition to new post-grant and PTAB procedures; Senate commentary emphasized retroactivity where Congress never gave jurisdiction previously (e.g., reexaminations).
